subject: Performance SLO qualification - Guardian AI - latency and cost levers
messages:

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: performance SLOs and next steps

Hi Sam --

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery on performance and SLOs so we have alignment before we run the worksheet:

- Target SLOs you called out: p95 latency <= 300ms for interactive chat, sustained throughput ~120 req/s, bursts to 200 req/s, expected concurrency ~50 active sessions. Streaming of token deltas required for UX (server-side chunked streaming).
- Model mix: primary is a 13B model for quality, open to evaluating 7B for lower-cost endpoints where quality is acceptable.
- Data plane: Guardian will need private VPC deployment for regulated customer data (we discussed Redwood Private).

Next steps I promised:
1) Send a filled SLO worksheet with a suggested performance configuration and cost levers.
2) Rishi to validate streaming and concurrency approach and recommend batching/cache settings.
3) Proposed next call: technical deep-dive + cost tradeoffs (Rishi + Marissa + your infra lead).

I've attached the SLO worksheet and a short overview of cost levers (quantization, continuous batching, caching, model variants). Please review and flag anything I missed.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Sam Kim <sam.kim@guardian-ai.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs and next steps

Thanks Marissa -- this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 300ms p95 target is for the text-generation chat flows (avg prompt ~120 tokens). For streaming we need token-level updates at ~100ms intervals to keep the UI smooth.
- Throughput: 120 req/s is the steady-state for phase 1, but by Q2 we expect ~300 req/s peak. For procurement we need a sense of cost at both 120 and 300 req/s points.
- Concurrency: 50 active sessions is fine, but many of those will be streaming concurrently which increases connection overhead.

Can Rishi confirm whether continuous batching + prefix caching will still hit the 300ms p95 for the 13B, or if we need to plan for model variants (13B primary + 7B fallback)? Also please include rough cost delta when using int8 vs int4 quantization if quality is acceptable.

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive next week.

--Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Kim <sam.kim@guardian-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs and next steps -- worksheet + recommendations

Sam --

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the completed SLO_worksheet.xlsx with numbers at 120 req/s and 300 req/s and the redwood-cost-levers.pdf with the short explanations. Summary highlights here:

- Likely configuration to meet p95 <= 300ms (13B primary):
  * Dedicated pools with reserved capacity for steady 120 req/s, autoscaling to handle bursts to 300 req/s.
  * Continuous batching configured with target batch latency 15ms and max batch size tuned per token-distribution -- reduces per-token GPU overhead.
  * Prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes (chat system prompts) estimated to reduce compute by ~25% for your workload mix.
  * Streaming: server-side chunked streaming + keep-alive connections; set concurrency target to 60 to account for streaming connection overhead.

- Cost / quantization tradeoffs (very rough):
  * 13B fp16 baseline. Int8 quantization typically reduces inference cost ~30-40% with minimal quality drop for most tasks; int4 can reduce another ~15-25% but may require quality A/B checks on your prompts.
  * Smaller 7B model as fallback can cut per-request GPU time by ~50-70% depending on prompt length and quality tolerance. We recommend model-split routing: 90% 13B, 10% 7B for low-risk flows initially, and expand as you validate.

- Operational levers that impact unit economics: batching, cache-hit rate, quantization profile, and reserved vs on-demand capacity. Worksheet includes cost buckets and assumptions.

Action items / next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm streaming-specific tuning (packet sizes, chunk interval, server-side buffering) and whether the continuous-batching config will keep p95 under 300ms for the 13B.
2) Guardian to provide a short prompt set (10-20 representative prompts) for a quick int8/int4 quality sweep.
3) Schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive next week -- propose Wed or Thu.

I've also added HubSpot notes and linked the worksheet: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: SLO_worksheet.xlsx; redwood-cost-levers.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Kim <sam.kim@guardian-ai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs and next steps -- streaming + batching note

Sam / Marissa -- quick technical note from my side:

- Continuous batching: For interactive chat with avg prompt length 120 tokens, we expect batching to amortize attention kernel overhead. With target batch latency ~15ms and adaptive batch sizing, p95 for the 13B on A100-style GPU should be ~220-280ms (including network overhead) assuming a cache-hit rate of ~20-30%. If cache-hit goes to 40% for repeated system prompts, p95 moves closer to 200ms.
- Streaming: Server-side chunked streaming at ~100ms intervals works; we recommend framing chunks at ~64 tokens or smaller. Keep-alive and connection pooling are important -- plan for slightly higher concurrency headroom (~+20%) to handle streaming tails.
- Quantization: Int8 is generally safe; int4 can be noisy for instruction-following prompts. We'll run a quick eval on your 10-20 prompt samples to measure quality delta. Expect cost reduction: int8 ~35% lower than fp16, int4 additional ~20% (highly workload dependent).
- Model routing: Recommend a primary 13B and a lower-cost 7B fallback for non-critical flows. For tight SLOs we can implement a fast-path using cached KV and smaller context windows for the 13B to avoid dropping to 7B too aggressively.

I'll bring concrete numbers to the deep-dive. Proposed times: Wed 11:00-12:00 PT or Thu 10:00-11:00 PT. What works for you?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
